45117-the-pony-rider-boys-in-new-england.title: An Exciting Quest in the Maine Wilderness
45117-the-pony-rider-boys-in-new-england.creator: Frank Gee Patchin
45117-the-pony-rider-boys-in-new-england.description: A book by Frank Gee Patchin. Oil of anise draws unwelcome visitors. Bees in force attack the Indian. What happened when the bear kissed Chunky. "Fat boy him up a tree." Tad ropes Mr. Bruin; then the fun begins. Boys take to the trees and Bruin takes the camp. Stacy's practical joke is exposed. "The boss bee was scouting me."  CHAPTER IX--BEAR STEAK FOR BREAKFAST Bruin causes a change of camp.

arxiv-2104-12582.title: Understanding and Avoiding AI Failures: A Practical Guide
arxiv-2104-12582.creator: Heather M. Williams, Roman V. Yampolskiy
arxiv-2104-12582.description: Abstract As AI technologies increase in capability and ubiquity, AI accidents are becoming more common. Based on normal accident theory, high reliability theory, and open systems theory, we create a framework for understanding the risks associated with AI applications. In addition, we also use AI safety principles to quantify the unique risks of increased intelligence and human-like qualities in AI.

arxiv-2203-16007.title: Multi-target Extractor and Detector for Unknown-number Speaker Diarization
arxiv-2203-16007.creator: Chin-Yi Cheng, Hung-Shin Lee, Yu Tsao, Hsin-Min Wang
arxiv-2203-16007.description: Abstract Strong representations of target speakers can help extract important information about speakers and detect corresponding temporal regions in multi-speaker conversations. In this study, we propose a neural architecture that simultaneously extracts speaker representations consistent with the speaker diarization objective and detects the presence of each speaker on a frame-by-frame basis regardless of the number of speakers in a conversation.

arxiv-2204-06816.title: Preliminary Results of a Survey on the Use of Self-Adaptation in Industry DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: The 17th Symposium on Software Engineering for Adaptive and Self-Managing Systems; May 21–29, 2022; Pittsburgh, PA, USA Price: 15.00 ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06 CCS: Software and its engineer
arxiv-2204-06816.creator: Danny Weyns 1,3 , Ilias Gerostathopoulos 2 , Nadeem Abbas 3 , Jesper Andersson 3 Stefan Biffl 4 , Premek Brada 5 , Tomas Bures 6 , Amleto Di Salle 7 Patricia Lago 2 , Angelika Musil 4,1 , Juergen Musil 4 and Patrizio Pelliccione 8
arxiv-2204-06816.description: Abstract . Self-adaptation equips a software system with a feedback loop that automates tasks that otherwise need to be performed by operators. Such feedback loops have found their way to a variety of practical applications, one typical example is an elastic cloud. Yet, the state of the practice in self-adaptation is currently not clear.

arxiv-2206-01363.title: First Observation of de Haas-van Alphen Effect and Fermi Surfaces in Unconventional Superconductor UTe 2
arxiv-2206-01363.creator: Dai Aoki 1, Hironori Sakai 2, Petr Opletal 2, Yoshifumi Tokiwa 2, Jun Ishizuka 3, Youichi Yanase 4, Hisatomo Harima 5, Ai Nakamura 1, Dexin Li 1, Yoshiya Homma 1 Yusei Shimizu 1, Georg Knebel 6, Jacques Flouquet 6, and Yoshinori Haga 2
arxiv-2206-01363.description: Abstract We report the first observation of the de Haas-van Alphen (dHvA) effect in the novel spin-triplet superconductor UTe 2 using high quality single crystals with the high residual resistivity ratio (RRR) over 200. The dHvA frequencies, named α \alpha and β \beta , are detected for the field directions between c c and a a -axes.

arxiv-2207-14221.title: Humans disagree with the IoU for measuring object detector localization error
arxiv-2207-14221.creator: Ombretta Strafforello, Vanathi Rajasekart, Osman S. Kayhan, Oana Inel, Jan van Gemert
arxiv-2207-14221.description: Abstract The localization quality of automatic object detectors is typically evaluated by the Intersection over Union (IoU) score. In this work, we show that humans have a different view on localization quality. To evaluate this, we conduct a survey with more than 70 participants.

arxiv-2208-04876.title: Optical throughput and sensitivity of JWST NIRSpec
arxiv-2208-04876.creator: Giovanna Giardino, Rachana Bhatawdekar, Stephan M. Birkmann, Pierre Ferruit, Timothy Rawle, Catarina Alves de Oliveira, Torsten Böker, Peter Jakobsen, Nimisha Kumari, Marcos López-Caniego, Nora Lützgendorf, Elena Manjavacas, Charles Proffitt, Marco Sirianni, Maurice Te Plate, Peter Zeidler
arxiv-2208-04876.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Giovanna Giardino, Rachana Bhatawdekar, Stephan M. Birkmann, Pierre Ferruit, Timothy Rawle, Catarina Alves de Oliveira, Torsten Böker, Peter Jakobsen, Nimisha Kumari, Marcos López-Caniego, Nora Lützgendorf, Elena Manjavacas, Charles Proffitt, Marco Sirianni, Maurice Te Plate, Peter Zeidler. To achieve its ambitious scientific goals, the Near-Infrared Spectrograph, NIRSpec, on board the Webb Space Telescope, needs to meet very demanding throughput requirements, here quantified in terms of photon-conversion efficiency (PCE).

arxiv-2209-04558.title: Persistent entanglement of valley exciton qubits in transition metal dichalcogenides integrated into a bimodal optical cavity
arxiv-2209-04558.creator: Borges H. S. 1 , Celso A.N. Júnior 2 , David S. Brandão 2 , Fujun Liu 2 , V. V. R. Pereira 2 , S.J. Xie 3, Fanyao Qu 1,4,‡, A.M. Alcalde 5,‡
arxiv-2209-04558.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Borges H. S. 1 , Celso A.N. Júnior 2 , David S. Brandão 2 , Fujun Liu 2 , V. V. R. Pereira 2 , S.J. Xie 3, Fanyao Qu 1,4,‡, A.M. Alcalde 5,‡. We report dissipative dynamics of two valley excitons residing in the K K and K ′ K^{\prime} -valleys of bare WSe 2 monolayer and the one being integrated into a bimodal optical cavity.

arxiv-2401-11569.title: Set-Valued Koopman Theory for Control Systems
arxiv-2401-11569.creator: Benoît Bonnet-Weill, Milan Korda
arxiv-2401-11569.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Benoît Bonnet-Weill, Milan Korda. In this paper, we introduce a new notion of Koopman operator which faithfully encodes the dynamics of controlled systems by leveraging the grammar of set-valued analysis. In this context, we propose meaningful generalisations of the Liouville and Perron-Frobenius operators, and show that they respectively coincide with proper set-valued analogues of the infinitesimal generator and dual operator of the Koopman semigroup.

arxiv-2407-17240.title: PrevaRank : Ranking Plausible Patches by Historic Feature Frequencies
arxiv-2407-17240.creator: Shifat Sahariar Bhuiyan, Abhishek Tiwari, Yu Pei, Carlo A. Furia
arxiv-2407-17240.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Shifat Sahariar Bhuiyan, Abhishek Tiwari, Yu Pei, Carlo A. Furia. Automated program repair (APR) techniques have achieved conspicuous progress, and are now capable of producing genuinely correct fixes in scenarios that were well beyond their capabilities only a few years ago. Nevertheless, even when an APR technique can find a correct fix for a bug, it still runs the risk of ranking the fix lower than other patches that are plausible (they pass all available tests) but incorrect.

arxiv-2501-03329.title: Field-Induced Ordered Phases in Anisotropic Spin-1/2 Kitaev Chains
arxiv-2501-03329.creator: Mandev Bhullar, Haoting Xu, Hae-Young Kee
arxiv-2501-03329.description: Abstract Motivated by intense research on two-dimensional spin-1/2 Kitaev materials, Kitaev spin chains and ladders, though geometrically limited, have been studied for their numerical simplicity and insights into extended Kitaev models. The phase diagrams under the magnetic field were also explored for these quasi-one dimensional models.

arxiv-2605-25890.title: Merge-Bench: Resolve Merge Conflicts with Large Language Models
arxiv-2605-25890.creator: Benedikt Schesch, Michael D. Ernst

europmc-pmc2721818.title: A distinct macrophage population mediates metastatic breast cancer cell extravasation, establishment and growth.
europmc-pmc2721818.creator: Qian B, Deng Y, Im JH, Muschel RJ, Zou Y, Li J, Lang RA, Pollard JW.
europmc-pmc2721818.description: Background The stromal microenvironment and particularly the macrophage component of primary tumors influence their malignant potential. However, at the metastatic site the role of these cells and their mechanism of actions for establishment and growth of metastases remain large

pmc-11289962.title: Overcoming the age-dependent SARS-CoV-2 vaccine response through hybrid immunity: analysis of humoral and cellular immunity with mass cytometry profiling
pmc-11289962.creator: Zayakhuu Gerelkhuu, Sehee Park, Kyoung Hwa Lee, Yong Chan Kim, Sook Jin Kwon, Kyoung-Ho Song, Eu Suk Kim, Young Goo Song, Yoon Soo Park, Jin Young Ahn, Jun Yong Choi, Won Suk Choi, Seongman Bae, Sung-Han Kim, Shin-Woo Kim, Ki Tae Kwon, Hye Won Jeong, Kyong Ran Peck, Eun-Suk Kang, June-Young Koh, Jae
pmc-11289962.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundAge-dependent immune responses to coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) vaccinations and breakthrough infections (BIs) in young and middle-aged individuals are unclear.MethodsThis nationwide multicenter prospective cohort study analyzed immune responses in participants of the ChAdOx1 (ChAd)-ChAd-mRNA vaccine group using cytometry by time-of-flight, anti-spike protein antibody (Sab) and anti-nucleocapsid antibody (Nab) titers, plaque reduction neutralization tests (PRNTs), and interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) release assays at various time points.ResultsWe evaluated 347 participants with an average age of 38.9 ± 9.4 years (range: 21–63).

pmc-11323446.title: Epigenome-wide association study on the plasma metabolome suggests self-regulation of the glycine and serine pathway through DNA methylation
pmc-11323446.creator: Jiafei Wu, Victoria Palasantzas, Sergio Andreu-Sánchez, Torsten Plösch, Sam Leonard, Shuang Li, Marc Jan Bonder, Harm-Jan Westra, Joyce van Meurs, Mohsen Ghanbari, Lude Franke, Alexandra Zhernakova, Jingyuan Fu, Joanne A. Hoogerland, Daria V. Zhernakova
pmc-11323446.description: BackgroundThe plasma metabolome reflects the physiological state of various biological processes and can serve as a proxy for disease risk. Plasma metabolite variation, influenced by genetic and epigenetic mechanisms, can also affect the cellular microenvironment and blood cell epigenetics. The interplay between the plasma metabolome and the blood cell epigenome remains elusive.

pmc-11348746.title: Comparison of gait analysis before and after unilateral total knee arthroplasty for knee osteoarthritis
pmc-11348746.creator: Jun Fukui, Yasumoto Matsui, Takafumi Mizuno, Tsuyoshi Watanabe, Marie Takemura, Shinya Ishizuka, Shiro Imagama, Hidenori Arai
pmc-11348746.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundGait ability can be objectively assessed using gait analysis. Three-dimensional gait analysis, the most commonly used analytical method, has limitations, such as a prolonged examination, high system costs, and inconsistently reported gait symmetry in patients with knee osteoarthritis (OA).

pmc-11429001.title: Use of recombinant proteins for the diagnosis and prevention of Mycoplasma bovis: a systematic review
pmc-11429001.creator: Camila Pachêco Gomes, Lucas Santana Coelho da Silva, Manoel Neres Santos Júnior, Maysa Santos Barbosa, Wanderson Souza Neves, Viviane Gomes Ribeiro, Bruno Lopes Bastos, Lucas Miranda Marques
pmc-11429001.description: IntroductionMycoplasma bovis is a highly contagious pathogen that causes various diseases in herd animals, negatively impacting reproduction, production, and milk yield. Effective diagnostic methods and vaccine development are critical for controlling M. bovis outbreaks. This systematic review aimed to evaluate diagnostic alternatives and vaccine compounds based on recombinant proteins.

pmc-11576640.title: Transitive reasoning in the adult domestic hen in a six-term series task
pmc-11576640.creator: R. Degrande, O. Amichaud, B. Piégu, F. Cornilleau, P. Jardat, V. H.B. Ferreira, V. Colson, L. Lansade, L. Calandreau
pmc-11576640.description: Transitive inference (TI) is a disjunctive syllogism that allows an individual to indirectly infer a relationship between two components, by knowing their respective relationship to a third component (if A > B and B > C, then A > C). The common procedure is the 5-term series task, in which individuals are tested on indirect, unlearned relations.

pmc-11630052.title: Rare imaging phenotype of late gadolinium enhancement in a patient with anoctamin 5 mutation
pmc-11630052.creator: Qi Zhang, Jinghui Li, Minjie Lu
pmc-11630052.description: ce imaging (MRI) revealed dilated cardiomyopathy, characterized by a rare late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) pattern mimicking ischaemic LGE, despite normal coronary arteries. Case presentation A 55-year-old female experienced intermittent dyspnoea, palpitations, and chest tightness over 10 years. Her 24-h Holter monitor revealed frequent premature ventricular contractions, sinus pauses, and second-degree sinoatrial block.

pmc-12468614.title: Expansion Microscopy of the Enteric Nervous System: A Feasibility Study
pmc-12468614.creator: Xin Xu, Wenchuan Zhang, Menachem Hanani, Kai-Christian Sonntag, Yu Xue
pmc-12468614.description: Expansion microscopy (ExM) enables conventional light microscopes to achieve nanoscale resolution by physically enlarging biological specimens. While ExM has been widely applied in neurobiology, it has not been adapted for the enteric nervous system (ENS). Here, we provide a detailed and reproducible protocol for applying ExM to mouse colonic ENS tissue.

pmc-12567915.title: Linking Atmospheric and Soil Contamination: A Comparative Study of PAHs and Metals in PM10 and Surface Soil near Urban Monitoring Stations
pmc-12567915.creator: Nikolina Račić, Stanko Ružičić, Gordana Pehnec, Ivana Jakovljević, Zdravka Sever Štrukil, Jasmina Rinkovec, Silva Žužul, Iva Smoljo, Željka Zgorelec, Mario Lovrić, Rafael Clemente
pmc-12567915.description: Understanding how atmospheric pollutants interact with soil pollution is essential for assessing long-term environmental and human health risks. This study compares concentrations of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and potentially toxic elements (PTEs) in PM10 and surface soil near air quality monitoring stations in Zagreb, Croatia.

pmc-12609491.title: Quadratic Spline Fitting for Robust Measurement of Thoracic Kyphosis Using Key Vertebral Landmarks
pmc-12609491.creator: Nikola Kirilov, Elena Bischoff, Yih-Kuen Jan
pmc-12609491.description: Objective: The purpose of this study is to present a kyphosis measurement method based on quadratic spline fitting through three key vertebral landmarks: T12, T8 and T4. This approach aims to capture thoracic spine curvature more continuously and accurately than traditional methods such as the Cobb angle and circle fitting.

pmc-12618457.title: Frailty as a predictor of mortality in lung cancer survivors: evidence from a nationally representative cohort NHIS 1997–2018
pmc-12618457.creator: Shu-chao Wang, Lei Peng
pmc-12618457.description: Frailty is a syndrome characterized by decreased physiological reserve and increased vulnerability to adverse health outcomes. Its impact on lung cancer survivors remains inadequately explored. This study examined the association between frailty and all-cause mortality in a nationally representative cohort. We analyzed data from the National Health Interview Survey (NHIS) (1997–2018) linked to the National Death Index through 2019.

pmc-13235057.title: Autologous tumor-immune effusion cocultures enable ex vivo functional profiling of radiotherapy-immunotherapy combinations
pmc-13235057.creator: Rebecca Zirnbauer, Daphni Ammon, Berta Mosleh, Nora Speiser, Anna Theophil, Markus Fabits, Mir Ali Reza Hoda, Michael Bergmann, Johannes Laengle
pmc-13235057.description: BackgroundCurrently, radiotherapy-immunotherapy (RT-IO) combinations provide limited and heterogeneous benefits in human solid cancers and are frequently selected empirically, partly because human models that preserve native autologous tumor-immune interactions are lacking. We developed patient-derived autologous tumor-immune effusion cocultures (PATECs) as an ex vivo platform to functionally evaluate RT-IO regimens within an immunocompetent tumor microenvironment.

pmc-13356862.title: Evaluation of a Portable Ultrasound System for Peripheral Intravenous Access: Performance and Safety in a Clinical Setting
pmc-13356862.creator: Matthew Kessel, Victor Ryan Bernal, Rebecca Galer-Siegfried, Trevor J Steele
pmc-13356862.description: BackgroundUltrasound-guided vascular access has been increasingly used in clinical practice with studies supporting improved insertion success and reduced complications. To meet the needs of various vascular access applications, ultrasound systems have been evolving with specific features. This study evaluated the safety and performance of a recently developed portable ultrasound system with needle tracking technology for peripheral intravenous catheterization.

pmc-13471217.title: Concordance of folate receptor expression in ovarian cancer over time: A single-institution retrospective study
pmc-13471217.creator: Mitra Abdollahi Neisani, Francis E. Marrero, Roberto Angeli-Morales, Sinan G. Khudhur, Kevin J. Wu, Yaohua Ma, Sophia G. Blumenfeld, Karina Hanna, Gerardo Colon-Otero, Aziza Nassar
pmc-13471217.description: BackgroundFolate receptor alpha (FRα) is frequently expressed in ovarian high-grade serous carcinomas and is a clinically actionable biomarker targeted by FDA-approved mirvetuximab soravtansine (MIRV) for platinum-resistant disease with high expression (≥75% of tumor cells with ≥2+ staining). However, longitudinal variability in FRα expression remains poorly understood. We evaluated temporal FRα expression changes in paired ovarian cancer specimens.
